title: One-coordinate hypercontractivity
statement: Let $P$ be a product of one finite probability space with strictly positive atom weights summing to one, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\lambda\le1$, $q>2$, and $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$. Assume every atom of $P$ has weight at least $\lambda$. For every real-valued function $f$ on the outcome space, both $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ hold, where $T_\rho$ is the product spectral noise operator and the norms are the corresponding product moment norms.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of one finite probability space with positive atom weights summing to one
Every atom weight is at least $\lambda$
$f$ is a real-valued function on the outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a probability law on a finite outcome space $\Omega$, with every atom of mass at least $\lambda>0$, where $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q>2$. For $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$, the operator $T_\rho f=\rho f+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_Pf$ satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every real $f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$.
